profile.entities: NIS Management Ltd (standalone, Kolkata, founded 1985, IPO Sep-2025); subsidiary NIS Facility Management Services Pvt Ltd (CCTV + housing-society security); Keertika Academy (DDU-GKY/skilling); Keertika Education Associates LLP (ITI training)
profile.mgmt: Debajit Choudhury (Managing Director, DIN 00932489); Kanad Mukherjee (CFO); moderator Parth Acharya (Kirin Advisors)
profile.subseg: Security services (46% rev); Housekeeping & payroll (39%); Integrated facility management + electronic security + CCTV rentals (13%); Other (skill development / course fees ~1%)
profile.themes: none (no exposure to Data-Center / Grid / Renewables / EV / Defence / Shipbuilding hardware themes)

deepdive.sec: Integrated Security & Facility Management Services (manpower-intensive B2B/B2G services; CCTV/electronic surveillance + skilling)

bull_bear.body:
- Conservative: prioritizes operating/free cash flow over topline; longer client tenure lowers indirect cost → improves cash generation to fund new-client acquisition.
- IPO cash currently parked (largely returned to balance sheet after temporary deployment); disciplined contract selection to protect DSO (avoid extended-credit central/state contracts).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Elevated receivables / DSO:** INR 145 cr consol; collection lumpiness from govt clients (DTET, Haldia Dock 5-month stuck bills, Patna, Irrigation) — mostly cleared Apr–May but recurring pattern.
- **Labour-Code cost crystallization:** WB draft rules pending; further provisions possible; pass-through assumption could be tested if clients resist.
- **Margin-mix dilution:** fast growth in low-margin security/HK vs stagnant high-margin CCTV/IFM.
- **CCTV STQC dependency:** "Make in India" certification device availability gates CCTV revenue timing.
- **Subsidiary drag:** NIS Facility Mgmt & Keertika de-grew; skilling revenue dependent on lumpy govt DDU-GKY/PMKVY awards.
- **Client / govt concentration:** WB ~70–75% of business; political/election-cycle fund freezes (vote-on-account) delay payments.
- **IPO-cash deployment execution:** large cash idle vs raised expectations.
- **Micro-cap / BSE-only liquidity** (issued shares ~1.98 cr; mcap ~INR 93 cr).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Candid, granular and conservative. CFO Mukherjee gave detailed contract-by-contract and receivables-aging walk-throughs; MD Choudhury repeatedly emphasized NOT chasing 30–40% growth at the expense of margin/cash — explicitly choosing quality over scale. Owned the muted growth and subsidiary de-growth transparently. Tone realistic on Labour-Code/STQC/WB-rules uncertainty ("still early days, wait a few quarters"). Mildly promotional only on the formalization tailwind and skilling optionality.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported-PAT collapse is entirely the INR 27.82 cr non-cash Labour-Code actuarial provision; underlying adjusted PAT INR 19.12 cr (Q4 INR 6.86 cr) — the operating business is steadily profitable.
- The real economic engine is annuity-like recurring monthly billing (no order book), so "incremental run-rate ~INR 10 cr/month" matters more than any contract-value headline.
- High-margin CCTV-rental capex from FY24/25 is now a ~INR 4 cr/yr EBITDA annuity that masked weakness elsewhere and is the swing factor for FY27 margin.
- The investment thesis is a regulatory bet: Labour Codes + STQC + GST formalization should price out informal contractors and re-route share to compliant players like NIS — but management itself flags a "sobering" offset (formalization compresses informal price umbrella).
- WB political change (new govt) is framed as a net positive (promised state investment + 40-yr local relationships) rather than a renewal risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Security services (46%):** largest, low EBITDA (4.5–4.8%), grew fast; full pass-through of wage/PF/ESIC/gratuity to clients.
- **Housekeeping & payroll (39%):** similar low-margin manpower-supply economics; fast-growing.
- **IFM + electronic security + CCTV rentals (13%):** higher-margin but stagnant/de-grew in FY26 due to STQC ("Make in India" CCTV certification) device stock-outs + WB election freeze; CCTV held ~INR 12 cr (of which ~INR 7 cr rental, ~INR 4 cr EBITDA).
- **NIS Facility Management Services (subsidiary):** CCTV (~INR 12 cr) + housing-society security; revenue fell INR 20→16 cr as wafer-thin housing-society contracts were exited.
- **Keertika Academy (skilling):** DDU-GKY (MP/WB) projects ended; revenue INR 4→2 cr; only Keertika school project running; DDU-GKY Odisha award expected June.
- **Keertika Education Associates LLP:** ITI training (4 ITIs), flat ~INR 4 cr.
- **Top clients:** Reliance Retail ~INR 30 cr (→35–36 cr); DTET ~INR 24 cr; Airport ~INR 22–23 cr; HDFC Bank ~INR 19 cr; Anjali Jewellers ~INR 12–13 cr.

latest_quarter.body:
- All contract-labour cost (minimum-wage hikes twice/yr, PF, ESIC, leave, gratuity) is **fully passed through to clients** — Labour Code 50%-of-gross-wage clause not yet causing client renegotiation pushback.
- EBITDA-margin lever is mix: CCTV/IFM (high margin, incl. ~INR 4 cr rental EBITDA) vs security/HK manpower (4.5–4.8%). FY26 margin expansion driven by the rental annuity.
- WB (~70–75% of business) draft Labour-Code rules not yet issued → future-cost uncertainty (new govt expected to publish rules).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol income INR 436.7 cr (+7.74%), Q4 INR 180.03 cr (+13.96%); FY26 EBITDA INR 33.53 cr @ 7.68% (+30 bps), Q4 9.41% (+115 bps); reported PAT hit by one-time INR 27.82 cr Labour-Code provision (adj FY26 PAT INR 19.12 cr, Q4 INR 6.86 cr); receivables INR 145 cr (consol); IPO unutilized INR 36.91 cr; ICRA BBB+ outlook upgraded to Positive; guidance: cross INR 500 cr / 12–15% growth FY27; CCTV & DDU-GKY (Odisha) recovery flagged.
- _Next Q → check: (1) revenue toward INR 500 cr & 12–15% growth; (2) CCTV revenue actually ramping by year-end + AMC wins; (3) DDU-GKY Odisha/Maharashtra/WB awards; (4) receivables/DSO trend (Haldia/DTET/govt collections); (5) IPO cash deployment progress; (6) WB Labour-Code draft rules & any further provisions; (7) EBITDA-margin mix (security/HK vs CCTV/IFM); (8) Calcutta Airport re-bid + Nabanna/New Secretariat renewals._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~12–15% consol growth; explicit target to cross INR 500 cr "within this financial year" (possibly with time to spare).
- **Margin:** Roughly sustain ~7–8% EBITDA; risk is mix — if low-margin security/housekeeping (4.5–4.8% EBITDA) outgrows high-margin CCTV/IFM, blended margin could slip; CCTV rental EBITDA (~INR 4 cr) recurs into FY27.
- **CCTV recovery:** Revenue from new CCTV tenders expected to start flowing "by year-end" (tenders in next 2–3 months, 3–4 month execution) + new AMC contracts at good margin.
- **Skilling optionality:** DDU-GKY Odisha expected to be awarded by June; Maharashtra & WB pending — flagged as a potential EBITDA "game changer."
- **IPO deployment:** significantly deploy remaining INR 36.91 cr this year; fully within 2 years.
- **Stance:** deliberately NOT chasing 30–40% topline (achievable via low-price tenders) to protect margins, DSO and free cash flow.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- No fixed "order book" — business is recurring monthly billing. Approx incremental run-rate adds ~INR 10 cr/month across new + expanded contracts.
- New/expanded FY26 wins: Haldia Dock (INR 50 lakh/month, 3 yrs ≈ INR 18 cr); Reliance Retail Gujarat (~150 stores, ~INR 1 cr) + retained Reliance WB (~250 stores, 14-yr client); Patna Secretariat (5-yr HK, INR 10.36 cr / ~INR 1 cr p.a.); WB Irrigation Dept (~INR 2 cr, 1 yr); New Town Smart City / Webel CCTV (INR 56 lakh); Mumbai Police CCTV (INR 1 cr); NESCO + PWD (post-election); NBDD (INR 10 lakh/month); bank branch expansions (HDFC incl. Arunachal, plus IndusInd & ICICI in North).
- Pipeline: more Webel / New Town Smart City / electricity-board CCTV work orders imminent; Calcutta Airport re-bid (lost earlier, INR ~15 cr p.a.); renewals due FY27 (Nabanna/New Secretariat, WB Govt).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Formalization tailwind:** Labour Codes consolidate 29 laws into 4; expected to squeeze informal/sub-scale operators and push govt/corporate clients toward compliant, audit-ready partners — NIS's core thesis ("the more the industry formalizes, the more we benefit").
- **CCTV/surveillance rebound:** STQC device availability improving + new govt (WB) + Maharashtra (Mumbai Police) entry → pent-up demand + AMC contracts.
- **Skill development (DDU-GKY / PMKVY):** dormant 2–3 yrs, now reviving; potential EBITDA game-changer if Odisha/Maharashtra/WB land.
- **Central-government expansion:** airports (credential-leveraged multi-state replication), NABARD, NBDD — short payment cycles, better net margins.
- **Geographic:** now 14 states / 14 branches / 18,000+ personnel / 1,500+ sites; Maharashtra entry via Mumbai Police.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: NIS is a 40-year-old, recently-IPO'd (Sep-2025) micro-cap integrated security & facility-management contractor whose FY26 was a "regulatory-transition" year: consolidated income grew a muted ~7.7% to INR 436.7 cr and EBITDA margin expanded ~30 bps to 7.68%, but reported PAT was crushed by a one-time non-cash INR 27.82 cr actuarial provision for the new Labour Codes (adjusted FY26 PAT INR 19.12 cr). The bull case is pure formalization-of-the-informal-sector plus deployment of unspent IPO cash — management targets crossing INR 500 cr and 12–15% growth in FY27, deliberately capping topline at 30–40% potential to protect margins, DSO and free cash flow.
